findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple missed hand washing opportunities:
1) One employee touched their hat, and donned a new pair of gloves without hand washing.
2) Another individual wearing gloves pulled up their pants and returned to food prep.
CORRECTED- times to wash hands were reviewed with the person in charge (PIC), who stated two new employees are on the line. An educational handout was provided by the inspector. Review times to wash hands with all employees, including, but not limited to: after touching ones self, after touching a cell phone, after handling money, after handling cleaning products, after taking the garbage out, and after changing tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

[P]

6-501.12 1) Floors were in general soiled under equipment throughout the back kitchen, dish area, and front make line. 
A. Single service articles, food debris, and general accumulation of soil were observed under the ice machine and thermolizers where roach activity was observed. 
B. Buildup of general grime and random items were observed around the water heater where roach activity was observed.
C. Heavy buildup of general debris was observed along the wall behind the dish machine.
D. Heavy buildup of general debris and other items were observed beneath the coffee counter and handwashing sink to the left of the 3 part sink.
E. Food debris was observed along walls and in corners under shelving in the walk-in cooler.
F. General buildup of food and debris was observed under coolers.
Thoroughly clean the floors throughout the facility. Ensure detail cleaning to eliminate potential food sources for roaches.

2) Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind the dish machine and beneath the 3 part sink. Attached plumbing at 3 part sink was also soiled with buildup of splash. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Wet mop was observed in the basin of the mop sink. Ensure proper storage of wet mops between uses to allow mop heads to dry properly.
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.114 (A) Old, unused salad chiller was observed in the back of facility by chemical storage. Unused equipment can serve as a hiding place for pests. Remove unused equipment from the premise.
The premise shall be free of items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Employee was observed rinsing their hands with the sprayer at the 3 part sink after changing out garbage can liners and just prior to returning to ware washing. Proper handwashing at designated handwashing sink was discussed. Employee washed hands at the handwashing sink prior to continuing with ware washing.
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.
If hands need to be rinsed, then they should be properly washed.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee working in dish area washed hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to getting paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with a reminder to dry hands with paper towels prior to using the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the faucet in order to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Ice machine had a chunk of black debris that appeared to be mold in the ice bin on the right side wall. Napkin was used to remove the debris. Covers were removed from the ice maker, and mold was observed on surfaces around water lines. The area where mold was observed was directly over an opening adjacent to the ice bin. Manager cleaned and sanitized the area where mold was observed during the inspection.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Wild rice soup in the front service line hot holding unit had an internal temperature of 127F. Soup was discarded and replaced with fresh product.  
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Greens and cheese slices in the Turbo Chef drive thru cooler were observed at 46F-50F. Based on information provided by the employee working in the area the cooler stopped working properly ~20 minutes prior. All TCS foods were moved to the drive thru salad and sandwich prep coolers that were holding foods below 40F.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Turbo Chef drive thru cooler was not on and had TCS foods inside (see #22 for details). Employee working in the area told the manager the light indicating power was on to the unit went out about 20 minutes prior. The cooler would not turn on. All foods were moved to properly functioning coolers. Cooler in question will not be used for storage of TCS foods until it is repaired and able to maintain foods at 41F/below. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution in sanitizer-bucket at front service line was observed to be soiled from use. Solution was replaced. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1. (REPEAT) Food debris and splash were observed in the bottom of coolers throughout, especially in the prep coolers. Clean inside coolers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
2. Shelving in both walk-in coolers were soiled with general buildup and debris. Manager noted the shelves are on the schedule to be cleaned.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12  1. (REPEAT) Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind and around clean equipment storage, behind the dish machine, and beneath the 3 part sink. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup. 
2. (REPEAT) Holes of various sizes were observed in the wall behind a storage rack to the left of the walk-in freezer. Repair options were discussed. Provide repairs that result in a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
3. Floors under and behind the dish machine and thermolizers were in need of cleaning. General buildup and debris accumulation were observed. Cleaning behind the thermolizer began during inspection.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness certification was available for one of the three CFMs on duty during the inspection. The manager with allergen training would be leaving as of 6pm at which time the facility will not have a CFM on-site with the required training. Manager noted other CFMs are in the process of completing certification. CFMs need to complete allergen training by next routine inspection to ensure there is always someone on-site during hours of operation with the certification.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:

Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.
If hands need to be rinsed, then they should be properly washed.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures

Soups were placed back in the thermolizer to reheat prior to hot holding for service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Food debris and splash were observed in the bottom of coolers throughout, especially in the prep coolers. Clean inside coolers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12  1. Wall at dish area was soiled with general buildup behind and around clean equipment storage, behind the dish machine, and beneath the 3 part sink. Ensure cleaning of walls throughout as needed to eliminate buildup.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Sanitizer at the 3 part sink dispenser was once again observed at improper concentration. Concentration observed for freshly dispensed sanitizer was at ~170 DDBSA/452 lactic acid. The effective concentration range for the product in use is 272-700ppm (DDBSA)/704-1875ppm (lactic acid). Sanitizer is also available at the dispenser by the mopsink. A spray bottle prepared using the mopsink dispenser was observed at a proper concentration of 700 DDBSA/1875 lactic acid. GM called the technician to request additional service for the dispenser located at the 3 part sink. The sanitizer at the 3 part sink dispenser does not consistently dispense at the proper concentration. The dispenser at the mopsink will be used for all sanitizer solutions until the dispenser at the 3 part sink is functioning properly and dispensing product at effective concentration required for use (see general comments for additional information).
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. If a chemical sanitizer is generated by a device located on-site at the food establishment it shall be used as specified in ¶¶(A) -(D) of this section and shall be produced by a device that is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Management was unaware the dish machine and sanitizer dispenser at the 3 part sink were not functioning properly until inspector pointed out the issues. Management was also unable to answer questions about the sanitizer that is now in use at the facility. A switch was made from quat sanitizer to a sanitizer with active ingredients of DDBSA and lactic acid (see general comments for additional information). Management was advised as to active managerial controls and being able to demonstrate knowledge related to equipment and chemicals used at the facility. A re-inspection will occur on 6/14/21 to verify proper function of the dish machine and sanitizer dispenser at which time the demonstration of knowledge pertaining to these items will be addressed. 
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink by coffee makers in back had a dark roast coffee dispenser in the basin. Coffee dispenser was removed from the basin.  
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of handsinks for any reason.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine was observed with a sanitizer concentration of 0ppm chlorine. Sanitizer bucket connected to the machine was full to the top and appeared new. Management was unsure as to when the chemical was changed, possibly the evening prior or sometime during the current operating day. After priming the line for several minutes and running additional cycles, the sanitizer concentration remained at 0ppm. Call for service was made, and a technician would be on-site the following day for repairs. In the meantime, the dishes could be washed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration as stated on the label instructions, and use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

Sanitizer was not properly dispensed at the 3 part sink dispenser. The lid was damaged on the chemical line, and suction was lacking. Even when sanitizer suctioned through the line and was dispensed it was observed at 0ppm. Sani-buckets and containers with ready to use wiping cloths registered at 0ppm DDBSA/lactic acid. Sanitizer was removed from the dispenser and mixed by hand to allow for proper concentration of 272-700ppm (DDBSA) and 704-1875ppm (lactic acid). Management was advised on mixing sanitizer by hand at the 3 part sink to use for manual sanitization until the dish machine is repaired and functioning properly.
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. If a chemical sanitizer is generated by a device located on-site at the food establishment it shall be used as specified in ¶¶(A) -(D) of this section and shall be produced by a device that is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

Containers with ready to use sanitizer wiping cloths were observed to be dry. Proper maintenance of ready to use wiping cloth containers was discussed. Ensure solutions are maintained in containers and proper concentration for sanitization is available. 
If a chemical sanitizer other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Dishes on drying racks in the dish area were not properly sanitized due to the lack of sanitization at the dish machine. All dishes were to be sanitized manually at the 3 part sink. All utensils and equipment were to be washed in the dish machine and manually sanitized at the 3 part sink until the dish machine was repaired and allowing for proper wash, rinse, and sanitize.
Utensils and food contact surfaces shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112 Thermometer was not present in the barista cooler. Ensure functioning thermometers are present in all cold holding units. 
Cold or hot holding equipment used for time/temperature  control for safety (TCS) food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sanitizer solution by barista station was murky and contained food debris. Solution was discarded and fresh sanitizer was provided. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of food debris and visible soil. Ensure sanitizer solution is changed as needed throughout the day once the solution becomes soiled and/or the concentration weakens.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Food debris and splash were observed in the bottom of all prep coolers as well as in the currently unused catering cooler. Clean the aforementioned coolers.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen awareness certification was not available for CFMs on duty at the time of inspection. Managers noted they took the allergen course. Copies of allergen certifications need to be maintained on-site.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.15: Employee in dish area was observed attempting to use a prep sink for the purposes of handwashing after being advised to wash hands between handling soiled and clean dishes. Employee was advised on handwashing at designated handsinks only. Employee washed hands at the designated handsink located at the opposite end of the dish area prior to proceeding with handling clean dishes. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Freshly prepared sani-bucket on the front service line was observed at 0ppm quat. Chemical container connected at the dispenser at the 3 part sink was observed empty, and the suction line was without product. New container of quat chemical was connected to the dispenser and observed at 200ppm when dispensed. All sani-buckets were changed and replaced with fresh product at proper concentration. 
Container with ready to use wipes was observed at less than 150ppm at the drive thru and was removed from the area. The container had a use by date of 12/7/20. Another container with ready to use wipes at the front counter (register area) was observed at 200ppm and made more recently (use be date in January 2021). Management was advised to monitor concentrations and maintain fresh product in ready to use wipe containers. Management was also encouraged to train all staff on basic troubleshooting and understanding what to look for regarding basic/proper function of the quat dispenser.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Handsink basin in back by coffee makers had funnels in it. Funnels were removed. Coffee grounds were also present. Discussed proper use of handsinks for handwashing only and cleaning frequency.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-602.11 Digital food thermometer was observed on the floor under the ice machine in back. Thermometer was replaced w/ a clean food thermometer. Ensure proper cleaning/sanitizing of food thermometers between uses as well as proper storage.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine sanitizing concentration was observed at 0ppm chlorine. New chemical bucket was recently connected to the machine, and product was not dispensing upon priming the line. Call for service was made to get dish machine repairs. Ensure dishes previously ran through dish machine are not used until properly cleaned and sanitized. *Call if machine is ready to be checked for re-inspection sooner. *
--Quat solution in sani-bucket at front counter was at 0ppm. Solution was remade and observed at 150-200ppm. Also, multi-use wipe buckets were observed w/concentration of 0ppm quat for wiping cloths, and one bucket up front was dry. Quat solution (200ppm) was added to both buckets. Ensure product in sani-bucket and multi-use wipe buckets are changed as needed and maintained at proper concentration per product label directions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 Spinach, cheese slices, and pickle chips were observed in Turbo Chef drive thru cooler that was off (67F). Foods were at 65F and left in cooler overnight. All foods were discarded. Ensure proper storage in cold holding units overnight; move foods to cooler that will remain on for overnight storage.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-202.12 Quat sanitizer was hooked up to the dispenser at the mopsink to a chemical line intended for bathroom disinfecting acid cleaner. Quat container was removed, and correct product was hooked up at the dispenser. Poisonous/toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer’s label use directions.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.13 Employee working in front service area was observed retrieving single use gloves to prepare food without  first washing his hands. Employee was also observed adjusting his hat just prior to retrieving the gloves. Employee was advised on handwashing and washed his hands prior to getting new gloves to continue with food handling.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed prior to putting on gloves and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Sani-bucket of single use wipes at the front service area was observed at 0ppm quat. Solution in sealed container with single use wiping cloths is supposed to hold concentration for 30 days and had a discard date of 12/9/19. Bucket was removed for solution and wiping cloths to be replaced. Bucket was sitting on a shelf by a cooler compressor, and manager wonders if elevated temperature in that area might effect the concentration as no other buckets had this issue. Manager was advised to check the concentration of the product in use periodically during the 30 day period of use to ensure proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Stem of digital food thermometer was soiled with food debris in storage case. Stem of food thermometer was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes or sanitizer wipes are used during temperature checks, then make sure stems are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed on the surfaces between the baffle and where it attaches in the ice machine. All other surfaces that were observed to be soiled the previous inspection were observed to be clean. Ensure cleaning of all surfaces as needed to eliminate mold buildup. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Sausage patties in drive thru hot holding were observed with internal temperature of 121F. Sausages were discarded and fresh sausage was cooked for remainder of breakfast service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

findings.title: Personal cleanliness
findings.citation_text:
2-303.11 Employee doing food prep was observed wearing a large watch. Ensure jewelry such as watches and bracelets are not worn during food prep/food handling. 
Except for a plain ring such as a wedding band, while preparing food, food employees may not wear jewelry including medical information jewelry on their arms and hands.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Sani-bucket used at barista area was observed at 200ppm but solution was soiled with debris. Solution was discarded and fresh sanitizer was provided. Ensure sani-bucket by barista area is changed frequently throughout the day as soil occurs. 
Chemical sanitizing solutions for wet wiping cloths shall be free of food debris and visible soil.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Clean knives were stored in the crevice between the knife storage rack and the wall. Manager removed all knives and placed them in the dish area for cleaning. Cease the practice of storing cleaned/sanitized knives in the crevice between the rack and the wall. This area is not considered a clean surface. 
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11 Plastic knives in storage container at bakery/cashier area were stored with handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. Store knives all facing one direction with handles presented out to avoid touching food contact surfaces when knives are retrieved by staff.
Single service and single use articles shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of food-and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Handsink in bakery packaging area was soiled with grimy buildup in the basin. Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed. 
--Wall under 3 part sink was soiled with buildup. Clean the wall and attached plumbing under the 3 part sink.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee in dish area was observed going between handling soiled and clean dishes without washing hands. Employee was advised on handwashing between handling soiled and clean dishes and was observed washing hands as needed for the remainder of inspection.
Employee working the drive thru window with a brace on her lower arm was observed handling her phone prior to retrieving a bag of single service lids to restock. Employee was observed getting a glove and was advised handwashing was required. Employee walked away and did not finish the task she began due to the need for handwashing/it being too complicated. The need for handwashing was revisited with employee prior to inspector leaving the area. 
Management was advised to reiterate proper handwashing and when to wash hands with all staff. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed inside the ice machine on the back side of the baffle as well and in and around the ceiling where ice comes out. Cleaning frequency was discussed, and manager began cleaning inside the ice machine during inspection. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

Mold buildup was observed along edges of the ice shoot on the lobby soda machine. Ice shoot was cleaned during the inspection.
Surfaces of equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned any time when contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Employee portioning foods on the front line had cheese slices stacked above the fill line in the sandwich cooler. Surface temperature was at 52F. Cheese slices were placed in another pan for proper storage.

Lettuce and spring mix in chillers was observed at 46F (internal temp at drive thru) and 49F-50F (surface temp at front make line). Manager noted just coming out of lunch the lids and drawers are often left open and/or opened and closed frequently. Also, the drawers on the front line chiller are not lined up properly to allow for ease in closing. Greens were to be used or discarded by 6pm. Manager was advised to closely monitor temperatures and keep drawers closed between uses to help maintain colder temperature. 

Products in the barista reach-in cooler had surface temperatures above 50F. Internal temperatures for milk and yogurt were observed at 55F-59F. The cooler was plugged in but not maintaining temperature (see #33 for details). All products that required refrigeration were discarded. Unopened products that didn't require refrigeration until after opening were moved to the walkin cooler. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 Carafes with milk and creamer at self service area were not labeled with a time stamp. Product was observed at 47F-48F. Manager noted it was likely put out around 1pm but a newer employee that didn't know to put a time stamp on it. Carafes were replaced with fresh product in properly labeled, chilled carafes. Manager was advised to make sure all staff know and understand the time control policy and marking carafes with a label when placed out for use. 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours food shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time frame for use and cannot exceed 4 hours. The food must be served or discarded within 4 hours.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Barista cooler was not maintaining proper temperature. Thermometer inside was observed around 60F. Cooler was plugged in but not running. The outlet reset to test mode. Manager reset the outlet to proper setting and plugged in the cooler to bring down the temperature after foods were relocated and/or discarded (see #22 for details). Cooler temperature began to drop during inspection. Food will not be restocked for holding until the unit is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Quat solution in sani-bucket on the front service line was not sufficient to submerge the wiping cloth. Solution was just prepared during inspection. Manager added more solution to allow for proper storage of wiping cloth. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Holder used for storage of the scoop at the main ice machine was soiled with dust and general buildup. Scoop holder was cleaned during the inspection. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Clean knife was stored in the crevice between the knife storage rack and the wall across from the dish area. Knife was placed at 3 part sink for ware washing. Ensure clean knives are stored properly in designated slots of the storage rack. The crevice between the rack and the wall is not considered a clean surface.
Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Containers holding plastic utensils up front were soiled with buildup of food crumbs under the slicer. Cleaning frequency was discussed, and holders were changed out during inspection.
Single service articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Condensation was observed dripping from the front fan on the condenser in the ceiling of the bakery walkin cooler. The bakers racks of food beneath were covered, but condensation was causing moisture accumulation on the covers and the floor in the cooler. Get the walkin cooler repaired to eliminate excess condensation, and be mindful of storage/general food protection.
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Upon completing handwashing process, an employee was observed drying hands with paper towels prior to shutting off the manual faucet. The same paper towels were then used to continue drying hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee and management.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. The last step of handwashing upon drying hands with paper towels should be to shut off the manual faucet. However, if additional drying is needed, then employees need to get new paper towels to finish drying hands. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Eggs and sausages in the hot holding wells at the drive thru were below 135F. Eggs were observed with internal temperatures of 113F and 126F, while sausage had internal temperatures of 103F-113F. All product was discarded and replaced with freshly prepared food.
Options for maintaining hotter temperatures at the drive thru hot holding wells were discussed. Cool air blowing in from opening the drive thru window may affect the holding temperature. However, the holding unit was observed set at 3, the products were double panned, and the pans with foods were not in direct contact with hot water. All of these were likely factors that resulted in the hot holding temperature dropping below 135F. Management was advised to work with staff to monitor and improve upon hot holding process at the drive thru.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Products in the Turbo Chef station cold rail on the make line were observed with temperatures above 41F. Sliced tomato was initially observed at 47F-48F. Manager noted the products were just placed in the cold rail prior to inspector's arrival. Upon checking temperatures in the Turbo Chef cold rail at the drive thru station those foods were observed at 36F-43F, and the rail was frosted up to help maintain temperature. The cold rail on the make line was not frosted. When temperatures were checked again ~30 minutes later tomatoes had an internal temperature of 50F; cheese was observed at 52F. All foods were moved to the cold holding drawer beneath, which was holding bean paste at 35F. Management will be calling for service to get the cold rail checked. Until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below the cold rail on the make line Turbo Chef station will not be used. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.18 Handsink in bakery area had black, grimy buildup along the top inside the basin. Cleaning frequency was discussed for handsinsks sinks and related fixtures.
Plumbing fixtures such as handwashing sinks shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Portions of chicken salad in the drive thru sandwich cooler had internal temperatures of 49°F and 47°F. Other products in the same cooler had surface and internal temperatures at 41°F-44°F. The temperature in the bottom of the cooler was at 35°F. The elevated temperature of the chicken salad was an anomaly and product was discarded. The cooler appeared to be working properly otherwise but may have been stressed from lunchtime use. Also new ovens for heating paninis are directly across from the cooler. Bags of ice were added in top of the cooler to help maintain colder temperatures. Management was advised to closely monitor the temperature of the unit and call for service if it appears to be failing. 

Foods had temperatures above 41°F in the top holding area of the salad cooler on the front line. Surface and internal temperatures were at 50°F-59°F. The top holding area was not on at the time of inspection. All foods were removed to be discarded, and the holding area was turned on to allow for proper cold holding. 

Cold foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at a proper product temperature of 41°F/below at all times during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Storage containers for clean equipment and utensils were observed to be soiled with varying degrees of food crumbs and general debris. Cleaning schedule for containers in question was discussed. Containers were switched out and cleaned during inspection. 

Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Single service knives on the front service line were observed with food contact surfaces extended up out of the storage container/ Store knives with handled presented up to avoid touching food contact surfaces when knives are being retrieved.

Single service articles shall be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Over easy eggs and egg whites in the drive thru hot holding unit had surface temperatures below 135°F. Internal temperatures were observed at 113-116°F (over easy) and 120°F (egg white). Products were discarded. A portion of scrambled eggs at the far left end of the same hot holding unit had surface and internal temperatures of 158°F and 166°F respectively. Products observed below 135°F may be experiencing temperature loss due the depth of the pans and/or because of their location in holding unit in relation to proximity of the drive thru window/general air circulation. 

Hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety (TCS) shall be maintained at 135°F/above at all times during storage, display, and service.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Food thermometers for checking soup were observed sitting on top of a rubber insulated glove (for removing thermolizer lids) soiled with splash/general buildup. At least one of the stems had what appeared to be stuck on food debris. Thermometers were removed from the area for cleaning and replaced with new thermometers. Glove was placed in dish area for cleaning.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Sanitize stems of food thermometers before and after temperature checks. Wash, rinse, and sanitize stems up to every 4hrs after continuous use. Store thermometers in clean cases or containers between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Surfaces inside dish machine were soiled with general buildup and lime. Clean and de-lime inside the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup.

Inner right wall of the ice machine had some black debris on it. Shift manager clean the wall inside the ice machine. Other surfaces behind the baffle were observed free of debris.

Knife storage case was soiled with crumbs/debris on inner surfaces. Case and knives inside were set aside to go through ware washing process. GM noted the case is cleaned once a week but will be cleaned more often to alleviate the issue.

Clean and sanitize the aforementioned items as needed at a frequency that will maintain them in a sanitary condition and eliminate buildup.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Bottom inside, drawers, and gaskets of most of the prep coolers were soiled with splash and food debris. 

Clean the prep coolers daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Bags of chicken and two jugs of juice were observed sitting in the back prep sink. GM noted they were thawing in water earlier, and the water was recently emptied from the sink. Cold running water was placed back on product until management was able to label and place products in the walkin cooler for storage.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the following methods. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier. GM had employee re-wash hands with proper technique.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

NOTE: Handwashing signage is posted at all handsinks, and other associates were observed washing hands with proper technique.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The knife storage case was soiled with crumbs/splash on inner surfaces. 

Clean and sanitize the knife storage case daily to eliminate buildup of splash and food debris.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Some mold accumulation was observed on the bottom right corner of the white baffle inside the ice machine. Condensation was dripping from the area into the ice. Manager cleaned the baffle and discarded a layer of ice. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as needed  to eliminate buildup of mold.

A soiled knife was observed in the top holding area of a sandwich cooler stored in the crevice between the edge of the pans and the outer edge of the cold well. The knife in question was taken to the dish area for cleaning. Cease the practice of storing utensils in the crevices of equipment.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Two employees working the front service line were observed washing hands without proper technique. The manual faucet was shut off without a proper barrier by one employee, and the handle of the paper towel dispenser was touched after hands were washed to retrieve paper towels by the other employee. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with staff; hands were re-washed with proper technique before returning to food handling.

Employees shall properly wash hands any time hands may have been contaminated, before putting on gloves/between glove changes, and before working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment:
750.830f - Three different types of slicing equipment were in clean storage tubs and observed with stuck on food debris (lemon, tomato, and cucumber). Equipment was cleaned and sanitized after morning prep and placed in the tubs. Manager took all items back to dish area to go through ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation. 
NOTE: If food debris and/or general soil remains, the items must be cleaned and sanitized again, as many times as necessary, to remove buildup and allow for proper cleaning and sanitizing of all surfaces.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Buildup of splash and food crumbs were observed in the bottom of storage bins for measuring spoons and other items in the clean equipment storage area across from the dish machine. Maintain storage bins clean to protect items from potential contamination.
 
Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 250 - Chicken and wild rice soup in the front counter steam table had surface and internal temperatures of 118F-119F and 124F-125F respectively. GM noted it was just heated fresh this morning and was potentially pulled from the thermolizer too soon. Soup was placed back in the thermolizer to reheat to 165F/above prior to being placed back in the steam table for service.

Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135F/above at all times during storage, display and service.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.citation_text:
750.180 - Packets of mac-n-cheese (cool to the touch & surface temperature below 100F) were observed in a pan of water heating in the hot holding unit at the drive thru. GM stated all hot foods are to be heated via the thermolizer prior to being placed in the front steam table or the hot holding units at the drive thru. GM was unsure as to when mac-n-cheese packets were placed in the hot holding unit and chose to discard all packets rather than placing product in the thermolizer for heating. 

All potentially hazardous foods shall be cooked to the proper product temperature using equipment intended for such purposes.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - An employee working at the front sandwich prep area was observed chewing gum. Employee discarded gum at the request of inspector.
 
Employees shall consume food, including gum and candy, only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside ice machine (mold on right inner wall next to baffle);  and
B) knife storage container in dish area (crumb buildup on top and in bottom) - removed for cleaning.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.160 - While waiting for a manger at the front counter, inspector observed an employee from the drive thru come up to pastry area to retrieve bagels. One hand was gloved while the other was not. The employee handled the bagels with her gloved hand but also touched her headset with the gloved hand prior to removing bagels from the slicer tray. Employee was later observed using ungloved hand to touch her headset. Proper use of gloves was discussed with manger to reiterate with staff.

Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Watch to make sure drive thru employees are not touching headsets with gloved hands and then using the same gloves to then handle ready to eat food.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Shell eggs in the reach-in cooler on the front service line had surface temperatures ranging from 44F to upwards of 52F. Staff noted the pan of eggs was recently out for use when egg patties were prepared. Cooler was holding below 41F, and the temperature of eggs began to slowly drop over time. Staff need to refrain from pulling large quantities of food from coolers during prep and only get out what is needed. Two dozen plus eggs sitting out of the cooler is not necessary. Only get out the eggs that are needed to prepare egg patties to avoid temperature abuse of shell eggs.

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage and service.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750.510, 512, & 1120 - A) Employee was observed handling a wiping cloth from a sani-bucket and then proceeded to handle a clean utensil and butter packets for an order. The same employee began to put on gloves without first washing hands to get a bagel. Handwashing was discussed, and the employee properly washed her hands prior to putting on gloves and continuing with food handling tasks.

B) Employee was observed retrieving gloves to handle pastries at cashier counter but did not wash hands. Manager called employee back to wash hands, and the employee was observed washing hands without proper technique - process lasted less than 20 seconds and faucet was shut off with bare hands prior to retrieving paper towels. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee.

C) Employee was observed wiping hands on cloth towel. Employee was advised to cease the practice of wiping hands on cloth towels of any kind. If hands need to be wiped, then they need to be properly washed. 

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and prior to handling food, clean equipment, or unwrapped single service articles. Common towels are prohibited for wiping hands.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Breakfast sandwich spatula was observed to be soiled with heavy food debris/grease accumulation. Staff on front line were unsure as to how long the spatula was in use and/or the last time it was switched out with a clean utensil. Spatula was taken to dish area to go through ware washing. 
Breakfast lasts longer than 4hrs. Make sure in-use food utensils and equipment are getting cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Clean lids were observed with buildup of splash on them. Lids were in a wall mounted wire rack located above the 3 part sink. Storage rack in question was too low and needs to be relocated to eliminate splash to clean equipment. Rack was moved up during the inspection.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Small flies (appeared to be fruit flies) were observed in varying numbers throughout the facility, with the majority (~12+) present at the bag storage area adjacent to the floor drain at the barista station. Three flies were observed on the wall behind the drive thru salad cooler, and one was observed by the motor under the drive thru soda machine. Four to five flies were observed under the 3 part sink near the buckets used for old coffee grounds storage. General cleaning and pest control were discussed.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed the probe thermometer to be soiled from previous use. Thermometer was cleaned during inspection. Please insure that utensils are left clean for the next use. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed a number of single-service cups holding single-service sugars etc at the drive-thru counter. Cease use of the cardboard/ paper cups. Use materials that are smooth and easily cleanable. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed a soiled knife block on the wall across from the dish machine. Also, observed the facility to NOT washing baking sheets inbetween multiple uses. While the majority of what the facility handles is non-potentially hazardous and parchment paper is used, the sheets should be sent through the wash, rinse, and santizing process when grease is involved (bacon) and accumulation of bread products is evident. Cease allowing food crumbs to accumulate on baking sheets. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the smoothie cube cooler to be soiled around the air return. Also, the shelving unit under the prep table by the walk-in cooler is observed soiled with grease, dust, and dirt.  Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed a large accumulation of drain flies around the dish machine area and the mop sink room. Drain flies have been previously noted around the self-service soda station and the coffee prep area of the front line. Only one pest was observed on the frontline during this inspection. Focus on the backline. See violation #42 as well. There seems to be a significant amount of ponding water and cardboard present around the dish machine and mop sink. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floors around the dish machine and mop sink to be soiled with an accumlation of water and soil. The lack of cleaning in these areas has led to drain fly proliferation. Complicating the cleaning concern, is the low grout between tiles in several areas. See that the floor is maintained clean and the tiles are regrouted as needed. The floor around the smoothie cooler is also observed soiled with accumulated fruit puree and splash. Finally, the floors in the walk-ins are observed with an accumlation of food splash, boxing materials, and ice in the walk-in freezer.   Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the wall around the smooth cube cooler to be soiled with food splash. Also, under the three compartment and preparation sink there is observed seriously food splash accumulation.  Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment: 750-1280 Observed an employee purse and gloves being stored intermingled on a storage shelf adjacent to the walk-in freezer. Moved during the inspection.   Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed a wet mop head to be stored within the sink basin. Store wet mops inverted or hanging so they can drip dry. Also, the room has bags of soiled linens and mop heads that are being stored close to the open flame of the water heater. This small room is packed full of materials. This practice may possibly be hindering the cleaning process. See that the mop room is kept clean. Pay attention to the storage of wet cloths (observed some of them on the ground behind the water heater). The premises shall be kept in such a condition to prevent the harborage or feeding of insects or rodents. 750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed the top shelf of the baking racks to be uncovered. Baked goods are not being protected from overhead contamination. Racks of goods that are being immediately and quickly wrapped or used do not need to be covered. Other goods that are going to be held in the backroom through a period of service should have the top baking sheet inverted. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed a serious accumulation of ice in the back of the walk-in freezer. The ice is observed ponding on a baking sheet (intended to hold the drips/ice) on the green shelving beneath the drip (no food being stored on this shelving) and onto the floor. The pile of ice on the floor is significant and will require effort to remove. A note was made during the previous inspection that AirMasters was going to be servicing the freezer. The manager made the comment that repairs will need to be conducted with a freezer truck on-hand. The facility's least busy period is the transition into fall/winter. See that the freezer is repaired so that ice no longer accumulates on the floor and shelving.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed a wet wiping cloth being stored on the counter between the two panini presses on the cookline. Moved to a sani-bucket during the inspection.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The following non-food contact surfaces are observed soiled: 1) shelf of cooler beneath the panini press (soiled with spilled food and grease); 2) the bread shelf over the sandwich prep cooler (food smear); 3) ice on shelves of the walk-in freezer; 4) the cabinets of the self-service soda station; and 5) within the dairy cooler under the drive-thru panini presses (parfait crumble crumbs). Clean these five non-food contact surfaces. Pay attention to the self-service soda station and remove any debris and water that may be providing a breeding ground for pests. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed a number of small flies around the self-service soda station. There were no pests observed within the kitchen. Facility was recently serviced by pest control specialists. See that the operators check the lobby and self-service station. These pests are normally observed around locations with water and soil. See that staff members are cleaning the counters, cabinets, and drainlines around this soda service area.  Effective measures to minimize the presence of insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 The walkway throughout the stored is observed clean. The flooring beneath eqiupment and along the wall-to-floor juncture is observed coated with grease/debris from mopping and general restaurant debris from daily operations. Observed the plumbing beneath the dish machine to be soiled with mold and dirt. The floor around the dish machine is observed soiled with grease and date marking labels. The corners under the dry storage shevling are observed dark from grease. There is observed a thick coating of ice in the walk-in freezer (this also presents a slip hazard). Finally, the floor around the water heater and mop sink is observed soiled with food debris, crumbs, and grease. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment: 750-1390 Mop cubby has several wet mop heads stored on the floor and within the mop sink. While there were no drain flies observed, this sort of practice does lead to providing a breeding ground for the pests. Cease storing the wet mop heads on the floor. Properly hang or invert mops to allow for proper drip drying. Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed the stems of three of the stem thermometers to be soiled with accumulated food debris. Stems were being stored in a well adjacent to the soup steamers. Manager stated that the stems only contact the exterior of the heated soup bags and the source of the food was not known. Keep these stems clean between uses. They are observed with significant food debris and obviously are contacting food at some point. Wiped clean during the inspection. Stem thermometers should be wiped clean after each use with a sani-cloth from a food -contact sani-bucket. The stems should be going through the wash, rinse, and sanitizing process at least every four hours while in-use.  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-650a One of the cutting boards, observed hanging on the hook right of the dishmachine, is observed so marred from use that food debris is stuck in the damaged/cut surface. Cutting board was pulled from use during the inspection. Discussed scrubbing of surfaces as part of the dish washing process. Either replace the board or make sure that surfaces are properly scrubbed. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750-820c Observed a soiled cup resting on the clean drain board. Soiled cup had food debris and sticker debris still attached to the interior and the exterior. The cup was pulled for cleaning during the inspection. Make sure that stickers are removed prior to or as part of the washing process. Check with dish washer to make sure monitoring of clean equipment is occurring. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed a wet wiping cloth being stored on a counter between bread slicing equipment. Moved to the sani-bucket during the inspection. Cease allowing cloths to rest on counters. Store cloths in sani-solution between uses.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the top and sides of the dish machine to be soiled with accumulated bread crumbs and food. Clean the dish machine. Also, observed the knives at the wall-mounted cutting board to have smears of food debris along two of the blades. Knives were pulled for cleaning during the inspection. It appears the knives are being wiped with a sani-cloth but not making it through to the wash, rinse, and sanitizing process. Make sure that if knives are being wiped with a sani-cloth while they are in-use, that they are making it through the washing process every four hours. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Overall, general surfaces are observed being routinely cleaned so they are in food condition. Detail cleaning is not occurring. Many hinges, edges, and ledges of shelving is observed soiled with accumulated soil and food debris. findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils

Remove the two containers for cleaning. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination. Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed a sani-bucket being stored on a top shelf over two lower shelves holding tomatoes about to be sliced. findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-510a Observed an employee changed tasks from handling cleaning equipment and soiled dishes to handling clean dishes. Dishes were sent through the dish machine again. findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-830 Observed dish machine to not be properly sanitizing dishes. Process was halted while Ecolab was contacted. Panera monitors the dish machine so failure occurred sometime after lunch. Noted that new detergent and sanitizing bottles are in place. During the inspection, Ecolab was able to attend to the machine.  All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed two containers (one holding frozen carton eggs and one holding frozen packed sausage mix) to be thawing under a single stream of water. Water stream was directly over sausage and water in container of egg was stagnant. It's difficult to properly thaw with a single-stream faucet especially when the items involved have two separate cooking temperatures. During the inspection, the faucet was moved to allow water to flow over both containers, however, manager eventually pulled egg product to allow sausage to thaw. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.
